## LitAnatomy v0.3.0

Bring in the review table you already keep, export your dissections for meetings and your thesis, and let the reading status keep itself up to date.

### Import your review spreadsheet
- **Add papers › From a spreadsheet…** (or drop the file on the window) reads an Excel (.xlsx, .xls), LibreOffice (.ods) or CSV file with a row per paper.
- You choose where each column goes: a paper's details (title, authors, year, DOI, journal, abstract, keywords, URL, citation key, tags, reading status, rating), a part of its anatomy (Contribution, Methodology, Limitations…), a **metric** named after the column (such as "Frequency Range"), or a **new field** named after the column. LitAnatomy guesses from the headings and contents. For example, "Why did they do" goes to Problem & Motivation, "How did they do" to Methodology, and a column of DOIs with no heading becomes the DOI.
- Your choices are remembered, so the next import of the same sheet is mapped already.
- With a DOI column, each DOI can be looked up online to fill in the authors, year and journal. The spreadsheet's own details are kept where the lookup has none.
- The usual import preview follows, with duplicates found. For papers already in your library, only their empty parts are filled in. Papers whose notes are imported become Reading or Summarised (see below).

### Export the dissections
- **Export notes…** in a collection or list (for every paper shown, or only the selected ones), and on a paper's page.
- **PDF:** a formatted document with a first page listing the papers and the pages they start on, then each paper with its details and parts. It has bookmarks to each paper and clickable DOIs, in the app's own fonts.
- **Word (.docx):** headings per paper and per part, metrics as a table and quotes as quotations, ready to edit.
- **Excel (.xlsx) and CSV:** a row per paper and a column per part, with a column for each metric. The Excel file can be imported again.
- **Markdown**, for notes apps and version control.
- Options: include abstracts, show the parts not written yet, and start each paper on a new page.

### Reading status
- A paper becomes **Reading** once you write one part of its anatomy, and **Summarised** once every part is written. It never moves back, so a status you set yourself is kept. You can turn this off in Settings › Anatomy fields.
- On Home, click **To read**, **Reading** or **Summarised** to list those papers.

### Key Metrics
- The metrics table now uses the whole width of its card.
- A **Table | List** switch lets you write the metrics as a list instead, one `Name: value unit` per line (bullets and `=` work too). Each metric still becomes a column in the matrix.
